Two insurance quotes. Which would you choose?

Same driver, car, insurer and one-year collision coverage. Only the deductible changes.

Quote A · lower premium

$600 per year

$1,000

Deductible per covered accident

Quote B · more protection

$900 per year

$250

Deductible per covered accident

A covered accident causes $4,000 of damage. Who pays how much?

Quote AQuote B
Insurer pays$3,000$3,750
Driver pays toward repair$1,000$250
Driver’s premium + repair cost$1,600$1,150

With no accident, the premium is still paid: $600 versus $900. Better protection costs more, holding the other terms fixed.

Illustrative quotes, not offers from an insurer. Simplified covered collision with no policy-limit issue. Principle: Progressive: deductibles and premiums.

An option buyer also pays for a right. The writer collects the premium and accepts an obligation if assigned.

For exchange-traded options, NVIDIA is the underlying company, not the option seller. Writers trade through the clearing system. Insurance and exchange-traded options have different legal terms.

FINA 402 · LECTURE 13 · 09 / 16

Activity 1 · Read the contract · 2 points

FINA 402 · LECTURE 13 · 10 / 16

Buy the stock or buy an option?

Buy the stock at spot

  • You own the share.
  • You pay the full stock price today.
  • The share does not expire.
  • Your dollar gain follows the stock price change.

Buy a call

  • You buy a temporary right to buy the share.
  • You pay a smaller premium today.
  • You can lose the entire premium.
  • A small stock move can mean a large percentage gain—or loss.
Same underlying asset, different initial investment and risk. Compare both dollar P/L and percentage return.

Sell the call: the other side of the contract

European option on one NVIDIA share. Exercise only at expiration.

The writer must sell one share at the strike if the buyer exercises at expiration.

Maximum profit $15; uncovered call loss is unbounded.

FINA 402 · LECTURE 13 · 14 / 16

Sell the put: the other side of the contract

European option on one NVIDIA share. Exercise only at expiration.

The writer must buy one share at the strike if the buyer exercises at expiration.

Maximum profit $10; maximum loss $190 if the stock falls to zero.

Four positions: payoff and P/L

FINA 402 · LECTURE 13 · 16 / 16

Key points · what to remember

1. A right—not the stock

A call gives the right to buy; a put gives the right to sell. The buyer pays a premium. Exercise only at expiration.

2. Payoff is not profit

A positive payoff can still mean a loss after paying the premium.

3. Compare returns fairly

Use each position’s own initial cost. A larger percentage return does not necessarily mean a larger dollar gain.

4. The premium can be lost

If the call expires unused, its buyer loses the entire premium. The writer takes the opposite side of the payoff.
